build: OUG disk crack, both trainers declined

comments.text: LEVELF sprite slots for VIC pointers $80–$8F in bank $4000. Each slot has 63 pixel bytes followed by a byte outside the VIC's sprite fetch.
The byte at $6001 belongs to the first sprite's 63-byte pattern. The stage loader uses this address for the length high byte before overwriting it with expanded sprite data.

The first 128 glyphs for LEVELF. The IRQ at $0C84 selects the 2 KB character set with $D018 = $0E while VIC bank $4000 is selected.
The low page of the playfield character set continues here, starting at glyph $1B. The VIC reads eight pattern bytes per glyph.

Eight-byte glyph patterns for indices $35 through $7F. The VIC fetches them from the playfield character set at $7800 when those character codes appear on screen.
LEVELF's glyphs $80-$FF continue the character set at $7800. Each glyph occupies eight bytes.

Remaining header bytes before the tile-patch pointer. The loader's stage-zero decision reads byte $C00A at $32DB.

Holds 20 ten-byte descriptors selected by the resident routine at $1965. The last two bytes of each record are the routine address read at $1DC9 and $1DCE.
Holds 104 object records. Setup at $3765 reads column, row, type and flags. The row and column choose where the tile patch begins when flag $20 is set.
The first $FF in the column field ends LEVELF's object list at $3773. The final record is four bytes of $FF.
Initialize the viewport row to $86 in $46 and its column to $05 in $45. Store the row plus $19 in $E690 and the column plus $1E in $E630. Clear $1D, $1F and $390C and return with carry set.
Return immediately from the actor callback. The corresponding descriptor slot passes control through $15EB and this RTS returns to the engine.
Forward the resident engine's stage update callback to $C5FE.
The 13 pointers index LEVELF's rectangular tile patches. $37B1 reads the low byte and $37B6 reads the next byte for the high byte.

Store $FF in the current actor's $EA50 field.
Initialize LEVELF actor type $32 in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.

Initialize LEVELF actor type $36 in slot X. Store $09 in horizontal extent. Store $10 in vertical extent, horizontal movement. Store $03 in $E9F0. Set the vertical overlap extent at $EA80 and the separate sprite colour at $E930 to five. Store $0F in $E870.
Clear actor visibility bit $40.

Initialize LEVELF actor type $35 in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $08 in horizontal movement. Set $EB10 to $80 to select direct sprite shapes. Store $0C in sprite colour.
Initialize LEVELF actor type $31 in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $0E in sprite colour.
Set extents two and three and $EA50 to $FF. If the low three actor flag bits are nonzero, save them in $E840 and clear them.
Set $20 in the actor flags in A and continue at the common initializer's store at $C489.
Initialize LEVELF actor type $2C in slot X. Apply $20 with OR to actor flags.

Call $2927 on the selected random branch. Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to three and two and extents to ten and eighteen. Set $E870 to four plus two random bits, colour five, direct shape $91 and actor flag $04. Clear the horizontal movement and counters at $E840, $E9C0 and $E750.
Continue the type $2D initialization after the optional common update. The timer expiry path at $C6CA uses this entry after calling $2927.
Set $EA50 to $FF and both extents to three, then transfer nonzero low actor flag bits to $E840 and clear them.
Write extent values three and two and then enter $C41B, which makes both extents three before transferring flags.
Write extent values two and ten and then enter $C41B, which overwrites both with three.
Set colour fourteen, $E9C0 to $14, bit $10 at $EB10 and extents sixteen and twenty-one. Clear $EA80 for this slot and write four to the fixed $E9F0 address.

Initialize LEVELF actor types $2F, $30 in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0A in $E870.

Clear the shared phase at $C945, set movement five, extents $24 and $3F and clear $E9F0, $EA80, $1D, $1F and $E9C0. Apply $C50B and allocate types $27 through $2B with the parent's coordinates and slot index.

Initialize LEVELF actor types $27, $28, $29, $2A, $2B in slot X. Apply $10 with OR to actor flags. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10. Store $0E in sprite colour. Store $FF in $EA50.
Set flag $10, set coarse Y to three and clear visibility flag $40.
Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to two and extents to ten and fifteen. Set $EA50 to $FF and hide the actor.
Decrement $E750. On underflow reload it to seven and toggle the low shape bit. Combine it with the group selected by direction and continue to the patrol update.

Set horizontal movement to $10, and check $275A, $E840 and $2760. The spawn request through $28AF additionally requires the random byte to be zero and uses type $2F. Then pass four in $08 to the turn routine.
Call $287A only when the playfield glyph animation phase is zero.
When bit $04 is clear, toggle the direction bit and set $04, then call $2757 with four.
Run the resident check and turn logic. When $E750 reaches zero reload it to five and increment the four-frame phase. Select the shape from $C5F5 using that phase and the direction bit.
Two four-frame groups of sprite pointers indexed by the animation phase plus the direction group's offset.
The update callback selected by LEVELF actor type $2C immediately returns to the engine.

Decrement the timer at $C68D. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C68E modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $7988–$79A7, replacing glyphs $31–$34 in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C62D. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $31–$34.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C629.

Clear horizontal movement, call $275A and advance the shape cycle. When the phase is zero, decrement $E840. A negative result selects movement $20, reloads $E840 to two, checks flag $04 and decrements $E870, using $C6CA for the reset.
Call $2927 before resetting the fields through $C3D6.
After $E750 underflows, reload it to five, decrement phase $E9C0 and apply incoming A as its reset value if negative. Use the phase and direction flag to choose and store a direct sprite pointer.
Four shape pointers for the direction with bit $08 set, indexed by the phase used at $C6F6.
Four pointers for the direction with bit $08 clear, selected by the same phase.

If $22E5 sets carry advance one coarse row and call $381A. Remove an actor with $E840 zero. Otherwise set its new type from $E840 plus $1A, remapping $20 to $25 with a nine-row correction. Call $3854 and clear removal. If the proximity tests pass, use relative coarse X to choose the $27DA parameter.
Call the resident checks and decrement $E9C0. On underflow reload it to $50. A successful $2760 check using $14 then spawns the four actors at $C794.
Mirror the actor flags and its horizontal extent to $7D and $7E. Remove on underflow of $E870 and otherwise call $287A.
Use $C7BD to allocate two vertical shots with opposing movement and two horizontal shots with magnitude $40, toggling direction on the fourth.
Allocate type $30, set its timer at $E870 to ten and copy the parent's four coordinate bytes using $22CC.

Call $38BD. While $390C is clear select colour four or two from $23B7. Carry from $275A sets $390C to $14, restores type $26 and clears visibility. Other paths select from $C939 and toggle direction and shared phase on $E9C0 underflow.
Use shared phase $C945 to read a shape from $C93B. Copy the parent position and add three to coarse X.
Use the shape pair at $C93D and follow the parent with $0280 added to its two-byte Y coordinate.
Use shape pair $C93F, follow the parent at coarse X plus three and two-byte Y plus $0280, and request type $2F through $28AF when the random byte is below eight.
Select a shape from $C941 and copy the parent position, adding five plus the incoming carry to coarse Y.
Select from $C943 and follow the parent at coarse X plus three. Apply ADC with five to coarse Y, using carry from the coarse X addition. Call $287A before the shared link check.
Copy the parent colour and remove the child when $390C is set or the parent ceases to be type $26.
Jump around the final flag test to the follower's return at $C938.
Remove the child if its parent's flags are zero or carry the removal flag, bit zero.
Pair of shape pointers for type $26, indexed by $C945.
Two shape pointers for the component offset on X only.
Two shape pointers for the component at Y plus $0280.
Two shape pointers for the component offset by three coarse X units and $0280 on Y.
Two shape pointers for the component whose coarse Y uses ADC with five.
Two shape pointers for the component with additions to both coarse coordinates.
Shared phase of the parent and its five linked components. Initialization clears it and the parent toggles it on timer underflow.
When $1F is set, increment the colour and set visibility. Test each active player unless $1D is negative, then call $216F and remove the actor if $23D6 succeeds.

When $1D is nonzero store its low seven bits at $70, set $1E to three and allocate replacement type $2C. Set the old slot's row to nine and copy its position into the new actor. Flag the old slot for removal, run $3854 for the new one and set $4F to $FF.
